Labeling rules (read first)
  1. Judge the file's primary responsibility from the verbatim source excerpt below. Ripgrep selects it from the current checkout; the byte range and source checksum are shown. A source revision and content digest that both match the bytes, plus a recorded workspace revision, make the excerpt source-bound. The workspace revision itself is recorded but not independently revalidated here. Unresolved/mismatched files are triage only. Generated summaries are deliberately not shown as evidence.
  2. Decide independently. Blind mode (default) hides the weak label and the proposed group until you choose, so they do not anchor you. Agreement with them is measured afterward, not assumed.
  3. One group per row from the list. Use a child group (database.postgresql, devops.env-config, devops.process-mgmt, frontend.sveltekit) only when certain; otherwise its top-level parent.
  4. Multiple responsibilities: pick the dominant one. If none dominates, choose AMBIGUOUS (counted, excluded from gold).
  5. Not a domain (run output, log, generated report, fixture data, memory dump): choose NOT_A_DOMAIN. Many rows under memory/runs are artifacts, not code.
  6. File gone or unreadable: choose SKIP.
  7. Review source-bound rows first. A source path with no excerpt, a binary file, a missing file, or a digest mismatch must be rebound or marked SKIP; do not promote a label from a filename or generated summary alone.
  8. Evidence completeness score (0–100) measures only provenance/excerpt completeness: safe file path 20, strict UTF-8 text 20, source-revision + content-digest match with workspace revision recorded 25, ripgrep declaration/metadata match 20 (fallback first nonempty line 10), and exact UTF-8 excerpt span checksum 15. It does not measure domain correctness or confidence.
  9. Support evidence annotation is your own explanation or a pointer to a relevant symbol/line. It is saved in this browser and exported with the review, but it is not source-verified evidence and does not raise the completeness score. For a source claim, cite an exact excerpt and line; do not paste generated summaries as if they came from the file.
  10. 8095 Tree-sitter/CST symbol observations are a proposal-only aid. Their returned byte spans are checked against exact current source bytes and the parser revision is shown. They do not establish the dataset's historical workspace revision, domain label, ontology mapping, or graph admission.
  11. Keep Blind mode on for labels intended for classifier gold. Visible-mode labels are recorded but excluded from gold evaluation. A distinct second reviewer on at least 10% of eligible rows is still required before trust.
